title: Contrast-Associated AKI — Prevention
sources: Critical Vector — CI-AKI Prevention (verified vs PRESERVE, AMACING, POSEIDON, Mehran risk score)
Mehran R et al. Risk score for contrast-induced nephropathy. JACC 2004
PRESERVE (Weisbord SD et al. NEJM 2018;n=5,177); AMACING (Nijssen EC et al. Lancet 2017;n=660); POSEIDON (Brar SS et al. Lancet 2014;n=396)
Cigarroa RG et al. Maximum acceptable contrast dose (MACD) formula

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV CI-AKI guide. Mehran score, the three trials, standard + LVEDP-guided hydration, drugs that work / don't, and the corrected MACD formula.

summary: IV isotonic saline is the ONLY proven intervention. N-acetylcysteine and bicarbonate-over-saline do not work (PRESERVE). Risk-stratify before the case (Mehran + contrast-volume-to-limit ratio), hydrate, minimise contrast, use iso-osmolar agent, avoid unmatched forced diuresis.

body.text: CI-AKI: serum creatinine rise ≥ 0.3 mg/dL or ≥ 25% within 48–72 h of intravascular contrast, no alternative explanation. Third most common cause of hospital-acquired AKI. Mechanisms: medullary hypoxia (contrast-induced renal vasoconstriction — the primary one) and direct tubular toxicity (worse with high-osmolar agents; iso-osmolar agents are significantly safer). Risk factors: eGFR < 60 (strongest predictor), diabetes, heart failure, high contrast volume, age > 75, anemia, intra-arterial delivery, pre-existing AKI.

rows: Hypotension (SBP < 80 for ≥ 1 h, or pressors / IABP within 24 h)

items: PRESERVE (NEJM 2018, n=5,177): bicarbonate NOT superior to saline (4.4% vs 4.7% MAKE); NAC NOT superior to placebo. Settled routine bicarb and NAC use.

AMACING (Lancet 2017, n=660, eGFR 30–59): no prehydration was non-inferior to prophylactic IV saline (2.7% vs 2.6%) with less fluid overload — challenges universal hydration in moderate-risk patients.
POSEIDON (Lancet 2014, n=396, CKD + ≥ 1 additional risk factor): LVEDP-guided hydration cut CI-AKI from 16.3% to 6.7% (59% RRR, NNT 11) vs a fixed 1.5 mL/kg/hr rate.

Standard: 0.9% NaCl 1.0–1.5 mL/kg/hr starting 3–6 h before contrast, through the procedure, then 1.0–1.5 mL/kg/hr for 6–24 h after the last injection. Target urine output > 150 mL/hr during and after as a marker of adequacy. Oral hydration is NOT equivalent to IV.

POSEIDON LVEDP-guided (preferred in the cath lab): 3 mL/kg 0.9% NaCl over 1 h before the procedure regardless of LVEDP, then post-procedure — LVEDP < 13 → 5 mL/kg/hr; 13–18 → 3 mL/kg/hr; > 18 → 1.5 mL/kg/hr — continued for 4 h.

rows: Works — Class I, the only proven intervention
Not superior; may be a convenience option for emergent procedures with short prep time
Harmful — forced diuresis without matched replacement worsens outcomes

body.text: Use the published Cigarroa formula: maximum acceptable contrast dose (MACD) = 5 × body weight (kg) ÷ serum creatinine (mg/dL), traditionally capped at 300 mL. (An eGFR term sometimes seen circulating is NOT in the real formula.) Keep the contrast-volume-to-MACD ratio < 1.0 — that ratio tracks with CI-AKI risk (Brown et al. 2010). Example: 80 kg, Cr 1.7 → 5 × 80 ÷ 1.7 = 235 mL.

items: 1. Identify risk before the case — Mehran score + contrast/MACD ratio, 90 seconds.
2. IV saline is the only proven intervention; use the LVEDP-guided protocol where available.
4. Use an iso-osmolar (or at least low-osmolar) contrast agent.
5. Hold nephrotoxins periprocedurally (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides) and don't add unmatched high-dose furosemide.
6. Metformin: hold at the time of contrast and restart 48 h later once renal function is confirmed stable (lactic-acidosis risk if AKI develops, not a CI-AKI cause itself).
7. Recheck creatinine at 48–72 h in at-risk patients before assuming they're in the clear.

buildNote: Tier 1. The Mehran risk score is an additive-calculator candidate (integer weights + published risk bands). Rule 6 (metformin) is added from standard practice, not the CV source.
